{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Australia|Cuisine of Australia]] 

'''Damper''' is Australian bushman's [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], made while camping or "waltzing matilda" (carrying a swag around looking for work). It is meant to be made outside by a campfire.

==Ingredients==

* 1 large [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[cookbook:Flour|self-raising flour]]
* 1 generous [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* scant ¼ cup [[cookbook:water|water]] (more and it will be as tough as an old boot)

==Procedure==
# Add salt to flour.
# Add water, then [[Cookbook:Mixing|mix]] and form into a round loaf.
# Dig a 1 foot-deep hole near a fire, and fill it with 2 shovels of hot coals and ash.
# Add damper mixture to a greased [[cookbook:Dutch Oven|camp oven]] (traditional cast iron round pot with lid).
# Cook in the hole for a maximum of 40 minutes. If undercooked it will be flat and rubbery.
# Your first try may be inedible. Keep trying, you'll soon be an expert.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* This cookbook also has a [[Cookbook:Drover's Damper|Drover's damper]] recipe.
* You can do this in a barbecue [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] with the mixture in greased metal foil as well. During cooking, damper increases in volume by ⅓ to ½, so allow room for expansion.
* If you aren't outdoors, just add mixture to greased oven tray and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in a moderate [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for 30–40 minutes.

==External Links==
*[http://www.australianoutdoors.com/damper.htm Australian Bush Damper] Gerry & Mo Noterey from Australian Outdoors (Variation recipes with pictures!)
*[http://www.discountcamping.com.au/index/products/campovens/cooking Camp Ovens Discount Camping]
*[http://www.millmerran.qld.gov.au/events/2006/Camp_Oven_Festival.shtml Australian Camp Oven Festival]
